---
title: "Recipe 4 — Write a CEL rule at S3 with a cost budget"
---

| Tool | Section | Level | Time | Layer | Tags |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [`cmd/trishula`](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/tree/main/cmd/trishula) + a rule pack file, any host with Go | Policy | medium | 10 min | engine · cel | cel, cost budget |

### Problem

You want one CEL rule at the S3 slot. You want a hard cost ceiling on it.
You want proof the ceiling bites, at evaluation and at compile.

### Solution

1. Copy the seed pack to a work file. Declare a budget below the rule's real cost
(the seed rule evaluates at cost 3):

```yaml
rules:
  - id: R4-BUDGET
    name: rate-shape-budget-bite
    description: 'The seed rate rule under a 2-cost ceiling'
    action: log
    costBudget: 2
    expression: |
      request.method == "POST" &&
      path.matches("/v1/chat/*") &&
      request.rate_windows["5m"].requests > 40
```

2. Run the pack. The ceiling stops every evaluation:

```bash
go run ./cmd/trishula --selftest --rules <pack-path>.yaml
```

```text
case below-threshold-no-match             match=false error=true  cost=3     FAIL detail=operation cancelled: actual cost limit exceeded
exit status 1
```

3. Check the compile side. The bundle load refuses an unusable declared budget
(the fail-closed gate):

```bash
go test ./internal/operator -run TestLoadRejectsUnusableDeclaredBudget -count=1
```

```text
ok   github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/internal/operator  <seconds>s
```

### Discussion

The budget rides the pack wire: `costBudget` sits on the rule. The policy's
`celBudget` is the fallback ceiling. Rule budget wins. A budget change re-plans
the program; it never re-compiles the module. The refusal detail names the
ceiling: `actual cost limit exceeded`. The compile-side gate rejects a pack whose
rule cannot run under its declared budget. No bundle ships on refusal.

The rule rides the S3 slot: the same rate rule the parity walk prints at S3.
